title: Hosted API - Embeddings & Rerank Demo
next_steps: Alex to send pricing and benchmark spreadsheet by 2027-12-01
Priya to share test dataset and API keys for a 2-week pilot
Schedule pilot kickoff with Searchly engs week of 2027-12-06
action_items: Alex (Redwood AE): Send pricing + benchmark sheet by 2027-12-01
Priya (Redwood SE): Share sample Postman collection and quickstart script by 2027-11-30
Samir (Searchly): Provide 50 sample queries and relevance labels by 2027-12-02
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Searchly through the hosted embeddings + rerank workflow: indexing docs with embeddings, using the embeddings endpoint for ANN search, then calling the rerank endpoint for top-K reordering. Discussed latency/cost trade-offs, batching and KV cache, and enterprise controls (SOC 2, SSO, KMS). Agreed on a 2-week pilot using Searchly test data to validate relevance and cost targets.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got Samir, Jenna, Leo, thanks for the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya who's our solutions eng, Marta from CS will hop in for ops stuff.
[00:11] Samir (Searchly): Yep, thanks. we're excited - search relevance has regressed after last model bump and we want to see if embeddings+rerrank can help.
[00:22] Priya (SE): great, quick agenda: run through a hosted API walkthrough, show embeddings endpoint, ANN demo, then rerank endpoint and console observability. Will leave time for Qs.
[00:35] Jenna (Eng Manager): Sounds good. We have a timebox of ~45 min.
[00:42] Alex: cool. So first, basics: customers typically do a two-step flow with our hosted API - offload dense retrieval to the embeddings endpoint, do ANN with your vector store or our recommended approach, get top-K, then call our rerank endpoint to score and reorder.
[01:05] Samir: quick q - why not just use a single large model for retrieval? latency/cost?
[01:12] Priya: yep, retrieval-first is cheaper and faster. embeddings are small vector ops, so you get very low per-query cost. Rerank is smaller top-K context so you can use a stronger model but on limited tokens. It's latency/cost optimization.
[01:34] Leo (SRE): What about batching and KV cache - will rerank use the same KV cache stuff as generation endpoints? We saw weird cache evictions before.
[01:46] Priya: rerank is stateless per-request by default, but the platform has prefix/KV cache for streaming generative workloads. We do continuous batching at the runtime layer to improve throughput. For rerank we recommend small batch sizes if you need low p95 latency; for throughput testing you can increase batch to get better GPU utilization.
[02:10] Jenna: any concrete numbers? p95 for rerank top-10 on hosted?
[02:16] Priya: depends on model. For a medium reranker we typically see 150-250ms p95 on our Hosted tier for top-10 with 1-2 tokens per doc summary; for larger models maybe 400-600ms. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet.
[02:36] Samir: and cost delta vs just embeddings?
[02:40] Alex: embeddings are pennies per 1k; rerank depends on model size and tokens. With our Optimize tool we can recommend quantization and batching to hit cost targets.
[02:54] [03:00] Priya: demo time - I have a quick notebook. First call: POST /v1/embeddings with the docs, get vectors. Example shown, slight transcribe: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeds -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input": "doc text"}' - returns 1536-d vectors (depending on model).
[03:28] Priya: then use your vector DB (we have connectors to Pinecone and OpenSearch) for ANN and get top 100 candidates. For Searchly you'd probably do top 50 then filter.
[03:44] Jenna: we use Elastic currently but thinking of migrating to Pinecone for speed on vectors.
[03:49] Priya: we have vetted configs for Elastic/OpenSearch too. Note: Elastic sometimes returns slightly different neighbors due to index settings.
[03:58] [04:05] Priya: next step, call POST /v1/rerank with the query and the top-k candidates. We pass a structured payload: query, candidates, metadata. Response is a scored list. Example - rerank model uses cross-encoder style scoring so it sees query+doc.
[04:24] Samir: what's the payload size limits? we have big docs (2-3k tokens).
[04:30] Priya: we recommend chunking documents and storing chunks for retrieval; rerank should only receive the snippet context that matters. There's a hard limit on request size for hosted endpoints - will attach docs - but practically you should keep per-candidate tokens small to keep rerank latency low.
[04:52] Leo: security questions: do you support SSO, SAML, KMS? we have strict compliance reqs.
[04:58] Alex: yes, enterprise customers get SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. We're SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001 in progress. We'll send our security pack.
[05:13] Samir: is there a VPC/private option? we might need a VPC peering or private deployment for PII.
[05:18] Alex: Redwood Private exists for that - private control plane, customer-managed networking and optional on-prem. For hosted pilots we can do customer-managed key and stricter data retention controls.
[05:31] Jenna: model drift and quality monitoring, how do you track regressions after updates?
[05:35] Priya: we have Redwood Optimize which monitors quality metrics against eval prompt sets, can alert on regressions, and recommend quantization or model swaps. You can pin model versions for rollout policies.
[05:51] [06:00] Priya: switching to the console - live dashboard shows per-route latency, token cost, and a trace for each rerank call. You can filter by model, route, or token bucket.
[06:15] Priya: here's a sample trace where a rerank call was routed to a cheaper model variant due to capacity policy - you'll see the fallbacks. (screen share)
[06:28] Jenna: that's neat. Can we set rules to always prefer a given region?
[06:31] Priya: yes, policy routing can enforce region, tier, or latency targets.
[06:35] [07:00] Priya: quick note on embeddings vector dims - different models produce 512/1024/1536 dims. That impacts storage and ANN perf. Our Optimize can recommend quantization like int8 or product quant to reduce storage by up to 4x with small accuracy hit.
[07:18] Samir: about ANN - do you host the index or do we?
[07:22] Alex: you can self-host indices; we also offer managed index connectors and recommend cloud vector DBs. For strict compliance, customers keep indices in their VPC.
[07:33] Leo: SLOs - any SLA for hosted API?
[07:37] Alex: hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency. For pilot we'd run hosted but can discuss Dedicated if you hit production scale.
[07:50] Jenna: what's the onboarding time for a pilot?
[07:53] Marta (CS): usually 1-2 weeks to get keys, run initial indexing and baseline evals, then 2-week pilot for relevance tuning.
[08:03] Priya: ok live rerank example: I send query 'best noise cancelling headphones' and top 8 candidates in payload - rerank returns re-ordered list with scores. I'll show the request/response in the notebook.
[08:26] [08:40] Priya: small transcription slip: the endpoint is /v1/rerank, body: {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"...","text":"..."}],"metadata":{}}. Response includes scores and optional logits.
[08:55] Samir: do you expose raw logits for calibration?
[08:58] Priya: yes you can request full scoring details in the response.
[09:04] Leo: what about rate limits for rerank vs embeddings?
[09:07] Alex: rate limits are per-key and configurable for enterprise. Hosted default caps are in the docs; we can raise them for pilot.
[09:15] [09:30] Jenna: we have ~250 QPS during peak per shard, and avg doc size ~600 tokens, top-k 50. Is that realistic?
[09:40] Priya: for 250 QPS it's likely you need Dedicated or reserved capacity. But you could start with hosted and use caching/prefetching to reduce calls. Also consider hybrid - embeddings hosted, rerank on Dedicated.
[09:58] Samir: can we run offline reranking to pre-compute scores for frequent queries?
[10:02] Priya: yes, offline batch scoring is supported; you can write back scores or store precomputed reranks to reduce real-time cost.
[10:12] [10:30] Priya: note on evaluation - we'll run your 50 queries with labeled relevance in the pilot and report NDCG/precision@k and cost per query.
[10:41] Samir: good. any pitfalls you often see?
[10:44] Priya: big ones: unchunked long docs (blow up token count), too-large top-k, not using caching for mutable user history, and ignoring vector normalization differences between DBs. Also watch embedding dimensionality mismatch when switching models.
[11:05] [11:30] Jenna: security follow-up - can you provide pen-test / attestation docs and compliance SLAs?
[11:36] Alex: yes, will share SOC2 report stub and pen-test summary.
[11:42] Samir: timeline question - if pilot looks good, how fast to move to Dedicated?
[11:46] Alex: Dedicated procurement and capacity typically 4-8 weeks depending on commit size, but we've moved customers faster when needed.
[11:56] [12:10] Priya: closing the loop, I'll drop a Postman collection and a small node/python snippet to call embeddings + rerank. Also include a sample script to chunk docs and push to vector DBs.
[12:22] Jenna: thanks. can you show pricing ranges now?
[12:25] Alex: high-level ranges only - embeddings low per-1k tokens; rerank depends on model. we'll send a detailed sheet.
[12:33] Samir: last Q - does Redwood do model explainability for rerank decisions?
[12:38] Priya: we provide token-level attributions in the trace and a simple importance score per-field; for deeper explainability we can run diagnostic probes.
[12:49] [13:00] Alex: ok let's recap next steps - Alex will send pricing and benchmarks, Priya will share quickstart/postman and sample scripts, and Samir will provide label set. Marta will schedule pilot kickoff.
[13:17] Samir: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:20] Jenna: thanks.
[13:23] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up.
[13:28] [END]
